about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Donald Norcross

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027
statements.title: NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027
sentences: Mr. Chair, I rise in opposition to this amendment.
I will remind my colleagues that President Trump established DOGE last year, which resulted in cuts across the entire Federal workforce of over 280,000 employees.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027
statements.title: NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027
sentences: Mr. Chair, this bill authorizes funding levels for key defense programs, including $4.3 billion for helicopter procurement, $3.3 billion for the F-35 program, over $3.9 billion for ground combat vehicles, and over $4.9 billion for key weapon systems procurement.

Mr. Chair, this bill also addresses the risks and the costs of military modernization without sacrificing oversight, such as authorizing multiyear procurement for the F-15EX and the F-35 aircraft, conditional on procuring sufficient spares for each aircraft; requiring the Air Force to budget for procurement a sufficient number of E-7A aircraft; and authorizing multiyear procurement for key munitions, coupled with strong funding for the munitions industrial base.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 5408, FASTER LABOR CONTRACTS ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 5408, FASTER LABOR CONTRACTS ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, when a union wins more fair pay and better working conditions for its members, it sets the bar higher for everyone.
Even if you are not part of the union yourself, you can still thank organized labor for negotiating some of what is in your contract.
If we can't count on billionaires negotiating ethically, and we can't count on existing rules to stop employers from running out the clock, what can we count on?
My Faster Labor Contracts Act is what an unprecedented coalition of lawmakers, labor leaders, and workers across this great Nation are now fighting back with.
Yet, by leveling the playing field, the Faster Labor Contracts Act would be the most significant new protection for workers since before World War II.
Mr. Speaker, I thank Representative Bobby Scott and my friends on both sides of the aisle for helping get this Faster Labor Contracts Act to this point.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FLEXIBILITY FOR WORKERS EDUCATION ACT
statements.title: FLEXIBILITY FOR WORKERS EDUCATION ACT
sentences: In fact, we call those captive meetings now when they come in to preach why worker unions are bad, but they have to pay them now.
My amendment, Raise the Wage Act, would ensure all workers receive a long-overdue raise. $7.25 an hour is minimum wage.
We gave billion dollar giveaways to those in the top tax bracket, and we can't raise the minimum wage from $7.25 an hour.
We used to regularly have increases on a bipartisan basis since minimum wage started almost a half century ago.
Please, Mr. Speaker, we need to raise the minimum wage.
Raising the minimum wage is not only good for the worker, but for their families.
I urge those who introduced this to come up with language that would not allow that to happen.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to reject this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECT AMERICA'S WORKFORCE ACT
statements.title: PROTECT AMERICA'S WORKFORCE ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of H.R. 2550, a bill that would restore collective bargaining rights for all Federal employees.
Earlier this year, President Trump launched one of the largest attacks on labor in the history of the United States, on the working people who voted to join a union and have a voice.
That executive order stripped Federal workers of their collective bargaining rights.
A collective bargaining agreement is a contract between the people and the public entity.
Less than 24 hours ago, in this very room, we had a chance to immediately restore the collective bargaining rights just for the Department of Defense.
We need to remember that collective bargaining agreements are about a vote by the people.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: STREAMLINING PROCUREMENT FOR EFFECTIVE EXECUTION AND DELIVERY AND NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026
statements.title: STREAMLINING PROCUREMENT FOR EFFECTIVE EXECUTION AND DELIVERY AND NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026
sentences: Madam Chair, this authorizes funding levels for key defense programs including $7 billion for the most expensive defense program in the history of our country, the F-35, and over $800 million to make sure that we continue the E-7A aircraft which is needed so badly, particularly in the Pacific.
It extends the review, the assessment, and the reporting to Congress on the F-35 program by the Government Accountability Office, which is incredibly important.

Madam Chair, I thank Ranking Member Smith and Chairman Rogers for setting by example what it is like to work in a bipartisan fashion and to Chairman Wittman for what he does each and every day to make sure that we work together to make sure we support our warfighters.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I ask unanimous consent to amend the rule to make in order the amendment at the desk that protects against any cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
statements.title: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
sentences: They are the ones who are processing Social Security checks for our seniors.
Trump is revoking their union contracts, the contracts which they negotiated legally and tried to enforce.
Right there, carved into the wood, it says, ``Union,'' and that is what we have to have.
